title: Console Action Center: Reduce Dashboard Friction — Prototype Review & Stakeholder Synthesis
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Validate a compact ‘Action Center’ pattern that surfaces rollout status, high-cost alerts, and quick mitigation actions in one persistent panel to reduce cross-panel navigation and improve time-to-resolution for incidents and cost spikes. This ticket captures the outcome of the cross-functional prototype review (Design/PM/Eng/SRE) and the synthesis of stakeholder feedback, redlines, and next steps for handoff to engineering.
acceptance_criteria: Finalized component specs for Action Center header, status badges, and compact action list
Accessible keyboard and screen-reader flows documented and validated against a11y checklist
Visual redlines committed to token-ready CSS variables and delivered Figma frames for dev handoff
Prototype edge cases documented: many-rollouts, mixed-model-variants, and out-of-band fallback actions
Stakeholder sign-off recorded from PM (Rosa Martinez) and Eng lead (Dmitri Volkov) or a clear list of outstanding risks
comments: 2026-02-22 Maya Chen: Posted interactive Figma prototype and Loom walkthrough. Emphasis on single-panel resolution flows: view rollout, pause, rollback, run cost-estimate query. Asked for engineering feasibility review on live-action button latency.

2026-02-25 Arjun Patel: Engineering notes — backend needs an API for aggregated rollout state (proposal: /v1/rollouts/summary). Concern: adding live action buttons requires idempotency tokens; flagged as dependency ENG-17981.

2026-02-27 Rosa Martinez (PM): Requested that we surface cost delta (%) alongside absolute token spend, and that the panel show the model variant serving traffic. Asked for a compact drilldown to the cost insights panel.

2026-03-02 Accessibility review (K. O'Neill): Contrast of status badges failed AA for red/green-only indicators. Recommended adding labels and distinct shapes; requested keyboard focus visible ring and ARIA live region for status updates.

2026-03-04 Design review session notes: Stakeholders prefer vertical stacked actions vs crowded horizontal chips for touch devices. Trade-off: stacked list increases vertical real estate but improves tappability. Decision: stack by default on mobile, compact horizontal on desktop with overflow menu.

2026-03-06 Dmitri Volkov (Eng): Implementation feasibility OK. Proposed dev deliverables split: frontend components + integration epic ENG-18xxx. Raised potential perf impact when subscribing to many live rollout streams; suggested sample-rate (polling fallback) for non-critical refreshes.

2026-03-09 QA lead (Samira Khan): Added QA checklist items — verify rollback confirmation modal, ensure analytics event 'action_center.button_click' fires with rollout_id, smoke test on small to large orgs, verify token-metering labels match billing API outputs.

2026-03-12 Maya Chen: Updated redlines after visual polish pass; attached final Figma frames and CSS token mapping. Requested design handoff meeting week of 2026-03-15. Noted two remaining UX open questions: inline undo vs global rollback page, and how we indicate partially-successful actions.
2026-03-12 Arjun Patel: Marked dependency ENG-17981 and ENG-17982 in the ticket as blockers for action-button rollout. Agreed to scope a read-only MVP if APIs are not available for initial release.
next_steps: Schedule handoff meeting with Eng + PM (owner: Maya) — week of 2026-03-15
Deliver tokenized CSS redlines and component spec sheet to frontend engineers (owner: Maya) by 2026-03-14
If APIs unavailable, implement read-only variant for initial rollout and track follow-up epic for full action enablement
Resolve accessibility fixes and re-run contrast tests (owner: Arjun) before dev handoff
Add telemetry acceptance criteria to the dev ticket and map events to analytics schema
